name: The Greenwich Hotel
positioning: Design-led luxury hotel in Tribeca, co-owned by Robert De Niro, with a Japanese-inspired spa
best_for: Travelers who want a characterful base in Tribeca
Guests traveling with a dog or cat

facts.text: The hotel opened in Tribeca in April 2008.
Actor Robert De Niro, who grew up nearby, is one of the owners.
Original paintings by Robert De Niro Sr. hang on the hotel's walls.
The exterior is hand-made Pennsylvanian brick, crowned with cast bronze medallions based on historic New York City manhole cover designs.
The lobby floors were modeled on the terra-cotta flooring of a 14th-century Italian palazzo.
No two of the hotel's guest rooms and suites are alike.
Rooms are individually designed with custom furnishings, Siberian oak floors and handwoven rugs.
The Shibui Spa takes its cue from Japanese bathing rituals.
The indoor pool is in the basement, with no windows, and is softly lit by lanterns.
The Drawing Room has a wood-burning fireplace, walls lined with bookcases and a bar.
Locanda Verde, from chef Andrew Carmellini, serves breakfast, lunch and dinner.
Locanda Verde provides 24-hour room service for the hotel.

highlights.text: The Shibui Spa sits under the roof of a 250-year-old wood and bamboo farmhouse, reconstructed in the hotel by Japanese craftsmen.
The TriBeCa Penthouse occupies the top two floors; designer Axel Vervoort and architect Tatsuro Miki drew on the Japanese aesthetic of wabi to create it.
All stays include a house car for short trips within downtown NYC, on availability.
Well-behaved dogs and cats are welcome, with no additional fee or size limit.
The Drawing Room extends into an outdoor courtyard covered by a canopy of latticed vines.

considerations.text: Pet owners must sign a waiver at check-in, and pets should not be left unattended in guest rooms.
An extra twin bed or crib needs to be requested in advance.
WhataHotel notes the intimate boutique size means limited room inventory.
